Match the original's parting, thickness and curls. Otherwise keep the upper lip and chin smooth yellow. Dark skin shading, nose shadows and lip creases are not facial hair. Preserve a bald scalp where the source has one and do not invent hair hidden under a hat.
Preserve the original garment design, uniform type, fabric, colors, headgear, glasses, decorations, accessories, expression, gaze, pose, action, framing, lighting, background and painterly color treatment. WHERE THE SOURCE HAS A GARMENT COLLAR, retailor its neck opening and shoulder fit to the mascot rather than copying a narrow human neck opening. Keep the yellow creature's anatomy and large green-ringed black eyes; do not restore human skin, human nose or human ears. Never place the visible mouth above the moustache or turn the moustache into a second beard. Clean-shaven originals stay clean-shaven.
When the source actually has a moustache, show it as a distinct visible band of hair with fine painted hair texture ABOVE the mascot's existing grey lip and small mouth. The reference mascot's normal grey lip wedge or its shadow does not count as facial hair; do not merely recolor that lip and omit the moustache. Retain a narrow readable separation between the hair and mouth. Apply this only to genuinely visible source facial hair; clean-shaven sources retain the normal bare mascot mouth.

Widen and reshape that original opening naturally around the base while keeping its style, tabs, piping and badges. Collar front sits visibly in front of the lower neck; collar back sits behind it, with coherent perspective, contact shadow and fabric tension. No neck clipping through collar, pinched narrow ring, floating collar, broken seam or abrupt geometric junction. The creamy belly stays under opaque clothing wherever clothing is present; never add a cream/white bib on the neck. Respect this fit even for tiny advisor or pilot portraits; it does not authorize inventing clothes on bare figures.

Where the source has clothing at the neck, that garment meets the underside of a visibly rounded chin. There is no separate exposed vertical neck column between head and collar, including bald and three-quarter-view portraits. Bare or scarf-only sources retain their original clothing state.
The lower head silhouette curves inward toward its base instead of continuing down as parallel straight yellow sides. Raise and broaden an EXISTING collar and shoulders to meet that curved chin; do not insert an extra yellow neck roll underneath it or add a collar where the original has none.
Keep the source's fastening state: a buttoned closed standing collar remains closed and buttoned, with both front ends meeting naturally at the center seam. Do not turn a closed military collar into a deep V-neck or unbuttoned shirt. Preserve open lapels/shirt collars only where the original is actually open.
Preserve the source aspect ratio, crop and number of figures. Preserve real alpha transparency, photographic frames, note cards and existing decorative markings where present. A free-standing cutout bust plus a note is not a framed photo card. Keep the original head/shoulder crop inside that actual photo rectangle. This instruction applies only when the original has a photo frame; never add a frame or note to a standalone portrait. Preserve the actual source crest/badge outline and visual motif rather than substituting a familiar generic star, crossed weapons or other invented emblem. Polished painterly HOI4 finish, legible at the original in-game size. One source image to one asset. No comparison board, new text, label, watermark or extra figure.
For a photo card, the background INSIDE the original photo rectangle is OPAQUE photographic backing, including the areas between the character and the frame. Transparency belongs only OUTSIDE the complete card-and-note silhouette; never punch transparent holes into the photograph. For every source preserve its original lighting, including deliberately very dark faces and existing vignettes; do not turn a near-black silhouette variant into a brightly illuminated portrait.
For framed adviser cards, preserve only physical attachments actually present in the exact original. Do not invent pins, thumbtacks, rivets, staples, paperclips, clips or screws on the frame or cream note. Existing indistinct note markings remain texture, not new hardware or readable text.
When a tiny source cap badge or other ornament is indistinct, retain only its visible gold/dark shapes, outline, colours and embroidery footprint with natural material texture. Do not resolve an unreadable motif into a recognizable anchor, bird, crown, star or other named device that the exact source does not establish. This condition preserves every symbol that is actually clear in the original; it does not remove or replace a visible source emblem.

Keep all five existing people in their original positions, full/partial-body crops, gestures and overlapping silhouettes, including the gesturing figures on the left. Convert only their visible bodies/faces/hands to consistent round-headed yellow mascots, each with a short broad neck fitted to its own actual blue/red traditional clothing, striped trim, belts and original hats/headcloth. Preserve the snowy mountain background, pale blue sky and green foreground, source shadows and framing. Do not add or omit people, add a foreground mascot, invent hats or replace the scene with a studio portrait/card/note. Retain original clothing style, open/closed layers, actual accessories/fittings, head angle, gaze, expression, lighting and crop. Fit the compact near-round yellow mascot head to a VERY SHORT BROAD neck and broad mascot shoulders at the actual garment. Adapt collar circumference and shoulder position naturally;no long neck stalk, floating collar, cream bib or newly closed open V.
Final source-specific check: Retain the actual visible source facial hair with its correct extent and color; eyes, upper-lip moustache, source-shaped open or closed creature mouth, chin beard in that top-to-bottom order. No invented hair from shadows.
